newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan Sugar passes on 2,500T soyoil tender.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan Sugar passes on 2,500T soyoil tender.

text.p: State-owned Taiwan Sugar Corp on Friday passed on a tender for a 2,500-tonne shipment of soyoil as only one bidder showed up, company officials said.
The shipment would have been slated for delivery by the end of May, a company official said.
Taiwan Sugar requires three bidders for any tender.
Taiwan edible oil producers have been cutting their soybean imports and turning to soyoil imports as a result of the island's hog foot and mouth disease epidemic.

Since it erupted on March 20, the epidemic and mass slaughter of nearly three million hogs has caused a significant drop in the island's demand for soymeal feed, forcing edible oil producers to cut soybean crushing to trim soymeal inventories.
Soyoil production also has fallen as the crush rate has been reduced, forcing producers to turn to crude soyoil imports to make up for the shortfall.
Soybean crushing yields two main products, oil and soymeal. Crushing to produce oil would result in a fast-growing surplus of meal for which there is no demand, crushers explained.
